{{Jainism}}
'''Akalaṅka''' [<nowiki/>[[IAST]]: Akalaṅka] (also known as ''Akalaṅkadeva'' and ''Bhatta Akalaṅka'') was a Jain logician whose [[Sanskrit]]-language works are seen as landmarks in Indian logic.<ref name=Book/><ref>{{cite book |author=Ganga Ram Garg |title=Encyclopaedia of the Hindu World |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WjDcd0cTFxQC&pg=PA288 |year=1992 |publisher=Concept |isbn=978-81-7022-375-7 |page=288 }}</ref> He lived from 720 to 780 C. E. and belonged to the [[Digambara]] sect of [[Jainism]].<ref name=Book>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=64HXAAAAMAAJ|title=The Enlightened Vision of the Self|isbn=9788170272441|author1=Akalaṅka|last2=Goyal|first2=Devendra Kumar|date=2005-01-01|page=1,2|publisher=Radiant Publishers }}</ref>{{sfn|Singh|Baruah|2003|p=9}} His work ''Aṣṭaśatī'', a commentary on ''[[Aptamimamsa|Āptamīmaṃsa]]'' of [[Acharya Samantabhadra|Ācārya Samantabhadra]] deals mainly with ''Jaina'' logic. He was a contemporary of [[Rashtrakuta|Rāṣṭrakūta]] king [[Krishna I]]. He is the author of Tattvārtharājavārtika, a commentary on major Jaina text ''[[Tattvartha Sutra|Tattvārtha Sutra]]''. He greatly contributed to the development of the philosophy of ''[[Anekantavada|Anekāntavāda]]'' and is therefore called the "Master of Jain logic".{{sfn|Singh|Baruah|2003|p=110}}{{sfn|Singh|Mishra|2007|pp=9–13}}

==Life==
Akalaṅka flourished in 750 C. E.{{sfn|Vidyabhusana|2006|p=186}} He was aware of the contents of the ''Aṅgas'', although it cannot be said whether they represent an idea rather than a reality for him, and he also seems to have been the first [[Digambara]] to have introduced as a valid form of scriptural classification the division into ''kālika'' and ''utkālika'' texts which was also employed by the [[Śvetāmbara]]s.{{sfn|Dundas|2002|p=80}} He is mentioned as a logician and a contemporary of [[Subhatunga]] and [[Rashtrakuta|Rāṣṭrakūta]] king [[Krishna I]].{{sfn|Vidyabhusana|2006|p=186}}

The samādhi of Akalaṅka is located between [[Karanthai|Thurupammor and Karanthai]] villages, at a distance of 19&nbsp;km from Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu.

==Works==

The following Sanskrit-language works are attributed to Akalaṅka. Some of these are:{{sfn|Singh|Baruah|2003|p=32}}<ref>{{cite book |author=Sures Chandra Banerji |title=A Companion to Sanskrit Literature |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JkOAEdIsdUsC&pg=PA10 |year=1989 |publisher=Motilal Banarsidass |isbn=978-81-208-0063-2 |page=10 }}</ref>

# ''Laghīyastraya:'' A compendium of three small treatises - ''Pramāṇapraveśa'', ''Nayapraveśa'', and ''Pravacanapraveśa''.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Maya Dhawan |url=https://archive.org/details/siddhivinischayaofanantviracharyaanditsvrittiofbhattakalankadevamahendrakumarjain_202003_118_o/page/61/mode/2up?view=theater |title=Siddhi Vinischaya Of Anant Viracharya And Its Vritti Of Bhatt Akalanka Deva Mahendra Kumar Jain}}</ref>
# ''Pramānasaṅgraha'': A work on epistemology or ''pramāṇa.''
# ''Nyāyaviniścaya:'' A work dealing with perception, inference and pravacana.<ref name=":0" />
# ''Siddhiviniscaya-vivarana''
# ''Aṣṭaśatī'': A short but important commentary on [[Samantabhadra (Jain monk)|Samantabhadra]]'s [[Aptamimamsa]].<ref name=":0" />
# ''Tattvārtharājavārtika:'' A commentary on [[Tattvartha Sutra]] resembling to Nyāyavārtika of [[Udyotakara]]<ref name=":0" />
